text:
ellie: Heads-up — I want to propose a change to admission control for high saturation scenarios. Instead of hard rejects we should try a latency-budgeted soft-admit (degrade) path + short queueing window. Looking for quick feedback before we open an RFC.

chris: Can you sketch the behaviour? hard reject -> immediate 429. degrade -> allow request at lower model or token cap? queue -> short wait then process?

ellie: Right. Proposal in bullets: 1) If pool CPU/GPU utilization > 92%/90% we stop new long-running sessions. 2) For incoming requests we consult a per-customer latency budget. If budget available, route to degraded execution (fewer tokens, smaller model or aggressive quantized variant). If no budget, place in a short FIFO queue (max 250ms) with probabilistic admission when full. 3) Fall back to 429 only after queue timeout OR when degraded variants unavailable.

maya: Sounds sensible. Two concerns: fairness across high-volume customers, and correctness regressions when we auto-quantize aggressive variants. We need per-customer SLAs + a whitelist for strict customers.

raj: For fairness we could apply a simple token-leaky-bucket tied to reserved capacity. Each customer has a weighted share. During overload the admission controller enforces min-share and then proportionally degrades extra share.

ops-bot: [alert] gpu-pool-eu-west-2 at 94% util for 12m. p99 latency 1.9s (SLA 2.0s).

chris: Cost angle — degraded path still consumes tokens and costs. If we send more smaller-models we may save latency but increase token churn. Need simulated cost model.

ellie: Agree — we should run replay tests over last 7 days traffic and simulate variants. I added a quick config prototype to test harness:```json
{
  "admit_policy": "latency_budgeted",
  "queue_ms": 250,
  "degrade_strategies": ["shorten_max_tokens","preferred_small_model","kv_cache_reuse"],
  "probabilistic_drop": { "base_rate": 0.05, "scale_with_fill": true }
}
```

maya: Nice. Also add a safety flag for "no-quantize" customers. And an explicit metric: "pct_requests_degraded_by_customer" so we can alert if a customer hits >20% degraded.

raj: For canarying we can open the policy to 5% of incoming traffic globally, and 100% for test accounts. Track p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per request, cost per 1000 reqs, and quality regressions via eval hooks.

sasha: Implementation notes — admission controller changes touch the routing layer and the runtime. We should implement a thin policy service that returns an action for each request: { admit: true/false, mode: "normal|degrade|queue", target_model: "gpt-small-q8" }. This keeps runtime simple.

chris: Question about queueing: are we ok with a single global short queue vs per-pool per-region queue? Global queues introduce latency spikes if networking hiccups.

ellie: Prefer per-pool short queues with cross-pool backpressure signals for fairness. Also include a per-request hint TTL so we don't enque long-lived websocket sessions.

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] staged rollout plan created: canary=5% -> 25% -> 100% with metrics gates.

maya: Gate thresholds suggestion: if p99 latency increases >5% or degraded-requests >15% revert. Also add rollback if any customer sends a complaint via SSO-tagged alert.

raj: I'll own the simulation harness. Plan: replay traffic with 3 strategies (reject-first, degrade-first, queue-first) and compare 99th latency, cost delta, and customer fairness index. ETA two days.

sasha: I'll prep the policy service proto and runtime contract. Chris can you coordinate the cost model inputs from billing?

chris: Yep, will add cost/time-series for last 30d. Also will stub a dashboard showing per-customer degraded rate + p99.

ellie: Great. Action items summarized: 1) raj: replay sim (2d). 2) sasha: policy service prototype (3d). 3) chris: cost data + dashboard (2d). 4) maya: whitelist rules and alert thresholds (1d). We'll review sim results and decide whether to canary. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

sasha: One more thing — add an opt-in header for customers who want best-effort lower-cost mode. That will let PLG customers opt into degradations for cheaper pricing.

ellie: Good call. Add that to the RFC.

chris: Noted. I'll file a ticket for billing changes.

ops-bot: [note] meeting scheduled: "admission-policy sync" tomorrow 10:30 UTC.
